documents.title: ATL-88 — Decommission the legacy warehouse ETL
documents.content:
Key: ATL-88
Summary: Decommission the legacy warehouse ETL
Type: Epic
Status: In Progress
Priority: Medium
Project: Project Atlas (ATL)
Assignee: Grace Adeyemi
Reporter: Grace Adeyemi
Due date: 2026-11-12
Created: 2026-09-14
Updated: 2026-11-16
Labels: etl, warehouse, decommission
Components: Data Platform / Pipeline

Description

Atlas is retiring the hand-rolled nightly ETL that feeds the finance mart and replacing it with dbt models on the new warehouse. This issue tracks the decommission itself: freeze new jobs, migrate the remaining 14 models, then switch off the scheduler.

Current state: 11 of 14 models migrated. The three remaining are the currency conversion model, the revenue recognition model, and the nightly refund rollup. None of them are Phoenix work; they read from the finance mart, not from any billing ledger.

Due date 2026-11-12 has passed. The remaining models are blocked on a data-quality review of the currency conversion table, which is scheduled for 2026-11-19.
documents.author: Grace Adeyemi

documents.title: ATL-91 — Warehouse schema review for the finance mart
documents.content:
Key: ATL-91
Summary: Warehouse schema review for the finance mart
Type: Task
Status: In Review
Priority: Medium
Project: Project Atlas (ATL)
Assignee: Grace Adeyemi
Reporter: Grace Adeyemi
Due date: 2026-11-19
Created: 2026-11-02
Updated: 2026-11-16
Labels: schema, finance-mart
Components: Data Platform / Modeling

Description

Review the proposed star schema for the finance mart before the ETL cutover: fact tables for invoices and payments, dimensions for account, product, and period. The review looks for grain mistakes, missing keys, and anything that would force a rewrite after cutover.

The draft has one clear problem: the invoice fact table is at invoice-line grain but the dashboard queries assume invoice grain, so every total currently double-counts lines. Grace has a rewrite in review that flips it to invoice grain with a bridge table for line detail.

Target: approval on 2026-11-19 so the models can be migrated before the ETL scheduler is switched off.

documents.title: ATL-77 — Fix nightly ETL skew on the orders table
documents.content:
Key: ATL-77
Summary: Fix nightly ETL skew on the orders table
Type: Bug
Status: Done
Priority: High
Project: Project Atlas (ATL)
Assignee: Grace Adeyemi
Reporter: Grace Adeyemi
Due date: 2026-10-30
Created: 2026-10-21
Updated: 2026-10-30
Labels: etl, performance
Components: Data Platform / Pipeline

Description

The nightly ETL spent 70% of its runtime in three skewed partitions of the orders table, because one merchant accounts for 30% of all order rows. Repartitioned on order_id instead of merchant_id and the job dropped from 96 minutes to 22 minutes.

Fixed on 2026-10-30. The same skew pattern exists in the refunds table and is tracked as follow-up work in the ETL decommission epic.
documents.author: Grace Adeyemi

documents.title: Three models left, all blocked on the data-quality review
documents.content:
Status as of today: 11 of 14 models migrated. Currency conversion, revenue recognition, and the refund rollup are left, and all three wait on the currency conversion data-quality review on 2026-11-19.

The original 2026-11-12 due date is missed. New estimate for the decommission is 2026-11-26 assuming the review passes first time.

Anyone from the billing side reading this: Atlas does not touch the Phoenix ledgers. The refund rollup reads the finance mart, which is fed by Finance's own extracts, so there is no cutover risk either way. Grace can be reached at grace.adeyemi@northwind.example.
